content.title: About
content.content: Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) is a marine fish native to the cold waters of the North Atlantic. Wild‑caught and sold raw, it features firm white flesh, a moderate texture and a mild, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the world’s most important commercial fish species.
In the wild, cod can grow over 2 m long and weigh more than 100 kg, though most market specimens are much smaller.
Cod can change the colour of its skin to match depth and lighting, helping it avoid predators.
In Europe it is classic for fish‑and‑chips, while in Japan it is often served as sushi or sashimi.
Wild cod typically has a more pronounced flavor than farm‑raised fish.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cod provides lean, complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other fish, cod is low in total fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains selenium, iodine and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, cod still supplies beneficial EPA and DHA.

items.title: Contaminant risk
items.content: Wild cod may contain traces of heavy metals and PCBs; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Raw fish parasites
items.content: Raw cod can harbor parasites; home preparation should include freezing at –20 °C for at least 7 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cod can be enjoyed raw in sashimi, tartare or marinated dishes, as well as quickly pan‑seared, baked or poached. Avoid overcooking to keep the flesh tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cod in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or in an airtight container. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before use, check for a clean sea‑like aroma; discard if it smells strong or ammonia‑like.
